summary: A busy, locked or unopenable SQLite database during signature verdict reconciliation or the signature migration is retried and no longer persisted as signature-state-corrupt; a stopped migration no longer rewraps its own fault at each start; st replication signatures resume (a person or the fleet's fault agent) clears a persisted fault and wakes the migration; ordinary verdict passes (projection tail, admission, sealed export, startup) judge at most 8 writer loans and leave the rest due, the signature job drains a verdict backlog at 50% duty, and a trust-root change or a changed delegation queues its dependents a page (1024) per loan instead of in one transaction; a transient error that keeps recurring for 5 minutes shows in doctor as signature-storage-retrying, still unpersisted

schema.detail: No table or claim schema change. Resume clears the existing fault columns of claim_signature_migration. A requeue in progress is a meta row per link (claim_candidate_requeue:LINK).

rules.detail: No checkpoint or retention rule change. Verdict semantics are unchanged; only when each verdict is judged changes.

compatibility.detail: No wire or stored format change. New route POST /v1/signatures/resume; a bound harness may name only itself.

downtime.detail: None. A large verdict backlog (after a resume or a trust-root change) drains in the background at half duty; no pass holds the projection lock or the writer for more than a slice.

manual.detail: A member that already persisted a transient error as signature-state-corrupt keeps it until a person or the fleet's fault agent runs st replication signatures resume --reason TEXT on it.

recovery.detail: Revert the build: transient errors are persisted as faults again and the resume command is gone. A fault cleared by resume stays cleared.
